decisive_items: invagination of the descending colon into the sigmoid colon consistent with intussusception
Colonoscopy revealed a 5 × 5 cm exophytic mass at the descending–sigmoid junction occupying half of the lumen

Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen demonstrated a well-defined hypodense lesion measuring 4.6 × 3.4 cm with fat density in the sigmoid-colon wall protruding into the lumen, along with invagination of the descending colon into the sigmoid colon consistent with intussusception
response.rationale: The patient's symptoms and imaging studies are consistent with intussusception, which is further supported by the colonoscopy and CT findings of an exophytic mass and invagination of the descending colon into the sigmoid colon.

rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and colonoscopy findings could be consistent with inflammatory bowel disease, but the imaging studies are more suggestive of intussusception.
The patient's symptoms of colicky pain and mucopurulent discharge could be consistent with diverticulitis, but the colonoscopy and CT findings are more suggestive of intussusception.
The patient has a large exophytic mass in the sigmoid colon, but the normal carcinoembryonic antigen level and the imaging findings of invagination are more suggestive of intussusception than cancer.
